items.abstract: <jats:p>Many few-shot learning approaches depend on learning an encoder that can produce discriminative representations. Contrastive learning is one of the most effective representation learning methods. We explore contrastive learning to train an encoder to generate distinguishable and informative representations. Most current applications of contrastive learning only train a single representation for the downstream task. Rather than following this straightforward scheme, we propose a multi-level contrastive learning approach for few-shot learning problems. Specifically, contrastive losses are applied at different layers of an encoder to learn multiple representations from the encoder. Afterward, an ensemble is constructed to take advantage of the multiple representations. We evaluated the proposed method on two few-shot learning benchmark datasets. Our model achieved the new state-of-the-art results for both datasets, comparing to previous regular, ensemble, and contrastive learning (single representation) based approaches.</jats:p>
title: Multi-Level Contrastive Learning for Few-Shot Problems
